solution:
Let \(t = \log x\), so \(dt = \dfrac{1}{x}\, dx\).
\(\displaystyle \int \frac{(\log x)^n}{x}\, dx = \int t^n\, dt = \frac{t^{n+1}}{n+1} + c = \frac{(\log x)^{n+1}}{n+1} + c\) \((n \ne -1)\).

Note that \(\dfrac{1 + x}{x} = 1 + \dfrac{1}{x}\). Let \(t = x + \log x\), so \(dt = \left(1 + \dfrac{1}{x}\right) dx = \dfrac{1 + x}{x}\, dx\).
\(\displaystyle \int \frac{1 + x}{x\,\sin(x + \log x)}\, dx = \int \frac{dt}{\sin t} = \int \operatorname{cosec} t\, dt = \log\left|\tan \frac{t}{2}\right| + c = \log\left|\tan\!\left(\frac{x + \log x}{2}\right)\right| + c\).

Let \(t = \tan(x^2)\), so \(dt = 2x\,\sec^2(x^2)\, dx\), i.e. \(x\,\sec^2(x^2)\, dx = \dfrac{dt}{2}\).
\(\displaystyle \int \frac{x\,\sec^2(x^2)}{\sqrt{\tan^3(x^2)}}\, dx = \frac{1}{2}\int t^{-3/2}\, dt = \frac{1}{2}\cdot\frac{t^{-1/2}}{-1/2} = -\,t^{-1/2} = -\frac{1}{\sqrt{\tan(x^2)}} + c\).

[Textbook answer-key error: the printed key gives \(\frac{1}{3}(e^{3x}+1)\) with the \(\log\) dropped; the correct answer is \(\frac{1}{3}\log(e^{3x}+1)\). The answer below is correct.]

Let \(t = e^{3x} + 1\), so \(dt = 3e^{3x}\, dx\), i.e. \(e^{3x}\, dx = \dfrac{dt}{3}\).
\(\displaystyle \int \frac{e^{3x}}{e^{3x} + 1}\, dx = \frac{1}{3}\int \frac{dt}{t} = \frac{1}{3}\log|t| + c = \frac{1}{3}\log\!\left(e^{3x} + 1\right) + c\).

Note that \(\dfrac{x^2 + 2}{x^2 + 1} = 1 + \dfrac{1}{x^2 + 1}\). Let \(t = x + \tan^{-1} x\), so \(dt = \left(1 + \dfrac{1}{1 + x^2}\right) dx = \dfrac{x^2 + 2}{x^2 + 1}\, dx\).
\(\displaystyle \int \frac{x^2 + 2}{x^2 + 1}\, a^{x + \tan^{-1} x}\, dx = \int a^{t}\, dt = \frac{a^{t}}{\log a} + c = \frac{a^{x + \tan^{-1} x}}{\log a} + c\).

Let \(u = e^{x}\), so \(du = e^{x}\, dx\); the integral becomes \(\displaystyle \int \frac{\log(\sin u)}{\tan u}\, du = \int \log(\sin u)\cdot\frac{\cos u}{\sin u}\, du\).
Now let \(t = \log(\sin u)\), so \(dt = \dfrac{\cos u}{\sin u}\, du\).
\(\displaystyle \int t\, dt = \frac{t^2}{2} = \frac{1}{2}\big(\log(\sin e^{x})\big)^2 + c\).

Divide numerator and denominator by \(e^{x}\): \(\dfrac{e^{2x} + 1}{e^{2x} - 1} = \dfrac{e^{x} + e^{-x}}{e^{x} - e^{-x}}\). Since \(\dfrac{d}{dx}\big(e^{x} - e^{-x}\big) = e^{x} + e^{-x}\), put \(t = e^{x} - e^{-x}\).
\(\displaystyle \int \frac{e^{2x} + 1}{e^{2x} - 1}\, dx = \int \frac{dt}{t} = \log\left|e^{x} - e^{-x}\right| + c\).

Write \(\cos^3 x = (1 - \sin^2 x)\cos x\). Let \(t = \sin x\), \(dt = \cos x\, dx\).
\(\displaystyle \int \sin^4 x\,\cos^3 x\, dx = \int t^4 (1 - t^2)\, dt = \int (t^4 - t^6)\, dt = \frac{t^5}{5} - \frac{t^7}{7} = \frac{\sin^5 x}{5} - \frac{\sin^7 x}{7} + c\).

Multiply numerator and denominator by \(x^{11}\): \(\dfrac{1}{4x + 5x^{-11}} = \dfrac{x^{11}}{4x^{12} + 5}\). Let \(t = 4x^{12} + 5\), so \(dt = 48x^{11}\, dx\).
\(\displaystyle \int \frac{x^{11}}{4x^{12} + 5}\, dx = \frac{1}{48}\int \frac{dt}{t} = \frac{1}{48}\log\!\left(4x^{12} + 5\right) + c\).

Since \(e^{3\log x} = x^{3}\), the integral is \(\displaystyle \int \frac{x^{3}}{x^{4} + 1}\, dx\). Let \(t = x^{4} + 1\), so \(dt = 4x^{3}\, dx\).
\(\displaystyle = \frac{1}{4}\int \frac{dt}{t} = \frac{1}{4}\log\!\left(x^{4} + 1\right) + c\).

Write \(\sin x\cos x = \cos^2 x\,\tan x\), so \(\dfrac{\sqrt{\tan x}}{\sin x\,\cos x} = \dfrac{\sqrt{\tan x}}{\cos^2 x\,\tan x} = \dfrac{\sec^2 x}{\sqrt{\tan x}}\). Let \(t = \tan x\), \(dt = \sec^2 x\, dx\).
\(\displaystyle \int \frac{\sec^2 x}{\sqrt{\tan x}}\, dx = \int t^{-1/2}\, dt = 2\sqrt{t} = 2\sqrt{\tan x} + c\).

Since \((x - 1)^2 = x^2 - 2x + 1 = (x^2 + 1) - 2x\), we have \(\dfrac{(x - 1)^2}{(x^2 + 1)^2} = \dfrac{1}{x^2 + 1} - \dfrac{2x}{(x^2 + 1)^2}\).
Now \(\displaystyle \int \frac{dx}{x^2 + 1} = \tan^{-1} x\), and with \(t = x^2 + 1\), \(\displaystyle \int \frac{2x}{(x^2 + 1)^2}\, dx = -\frac{1}{x^2 + 1}\).
Hence the integral \(= \tan^{-1} x + \dfrac{1}{x^2 + 1} + c\).

Let \(t = 3\cos^2 x + 4\sin^2 x\). Then \(dt = (-6\cos x\sin x + 8\sin x\cos x)\, dx = 2\sin x\cos x\, dx\), which is exactly the numerator.
\(\displaystyle \int \frac{2\sin x\cos x}{3\cos^2 x + 4\sin^2 x}\, dx = \int \frac{dt}{t} = \log\!\left(3\cos^2 x + 4\sin^2 x\right) + c\).

Since \(\sqrt{x^3} = x\sqrt{x}\), we have \(\sqrt{x} + \sqrt{x^3} = \sqrt{x}\,(1 + x)\). Let \(t = \sqrt{x}\), so \(x = t^2\) and \(dx = 2t\, dt\).
\(\displaystyle \int \frac{1}{\sqrt{x}\,(1 + x)}\, dx = \int \frac{2t}{t\,(1 + t^2)}\, dt = \int \frac{2}{1 + t^2}\, dt = 2\tan^{-1} t = 2\tan^{-1}\!\sqrt{x} + c\).

The numerator is the derivative of the denominator: \(\dfrac{d}{dx}\big(10^{x} + x^{10}\big) = 10^{x}\log 10 + 10x^{9}\). Let \(t = 10^{x} + x^{10}\).
\(\displaystyle \int \frac{10x^{9} + 10^{x}\log 10}{10^{x} + x^{10}}\, dx = \int \frac{dt}{t} = \log\!\left(10^{x} + x^{10}\right) + c\).

Let \(t = 1 + 4x^{n}\), so \(dt = 4n\,x^{n-1}\, dx\), i.e. \(x^{n-1}\, dx = \dfrac{dt}{4n}\).
\(\displaystyle \int \frac{x^{n-1}}{\sqrt{1 + 4x^{n}}}\, dx = \frac{1}{4n}\int t^{-1/2}\, dt = \frac{1}{4n}\cdot 2\sqrt{t} = \frac{1}{2n}\sqrt{1 + 4x^{n}} + c\).

Let \(t = x^3\), so \(dt = 3x^2\, dx\); also \(x^6 = (x^3)^2 = t^2\).
\(\displaystyle \int \frac{x^2}{\sqrt{9 - x^6}}\, dx = \frac{1}{3}\int \frac{dt}{\sqrt{9 - t^2}} = \frac{1}{3}\sin^{-1}\!\frac{t}{3} = \frac{1}{3}\sin^{-1}\!\left(\frac{x^3}{3}\right) + c\).

Multiply numerator and denominator by \(x^2\): \(\dfrac{1}{x(x^3 - 1)} = \dfrac{x^2}{x^3(x^3 - 1)}\). Let \(t = x^3\), so \(dt = 3x^2\, dx\).
\(\displaystyle \int \frac{x^2}{x^3(x^3 - 1)}\, dx = \frac{1}{3}\int \frac{dt}{t(t - 1)} = \frac{1}{3}\int \left(\frac{1}{t - 1} - \frac{1}{t}\right) dt = \frac{1}{3}\log\left|\frac{t - 1}{t}\right| = \frac{1}{3}\log\left|\frac{x^3 - 1}{x^3}\right| + c\).

Let \(t = \log(\log x)\). Then \(dt = \dfrac{1}{\log x}\cdot\dfrac{1}{x}\, dx = \dfrac{1}{x\,\log x}\, dx\).
\(\displaystyle \int \frac{1}{x\,\log x\,\log(\log x)}\, dx = \int \frac{dt}{t} = \log\big|\log(\log x)\big| + c\).

Using sum-to-product formulae: \(\cos 3x - \cos 4x = 2\sin\dfrac{7x}{2}\sin\dfrac{x}{2}\) and \(\sin 3x + \sin 4x = 2\sin\dfrac{7x}{2}\cos\dfrac{x}{2}\).
So the integrand \(= \dfrac{2\sin\frac{7x}{2}\sin\frac{x}{2}}{2\sin\frac{7x}{2}\cos\frac{x}{2}} = \tan\dfrac{x}{2}\).
\(\displaystyle \int \tan\frac{x}{2}\, dx = -2\log\left|\cos\frac{x}{2}\right| + c\).

Write \(\cos x = \cos\big[(x - a) + a\big] = \cos(x - a)\cos a - \sin(x - a)\sin a\).
Then \(\dfrac{\cos x}{\sin(x - a)} = \cos a\,\dfrac{\cos(x - a)}{\sin(x - a)} - \sin a = \cos a\,\cot(x - a) - \sin a\).
\(\displaystyle \int \frac{\cos x}{\sin(x - a)}\, dx = \cos a\,\log|\sin(x - a)| - x\sin a + c\).

Write \(x - a = (x + b) - (a + b)\), so \(\sin(x - a) = \sin(x + b)\cos(a + b) - \cos(x + b)\sin(a + b)\).
Then \(\dfrac{\sin(x - a)}{\cos(x + b)} = \cos(a + b)\,\tan(x + b) - \sin(a + b)\).
\(\displaystyle \int \frac{\sin(x - a)}{\cos(x + b)}\, dx = -\cos(a + b)\,\log|\cos(x + b)| - x\sin(a + b) + c\).

Factor the denominator: \(\sin x\cos x + 2\cos^2 x = \cos^2 x\,(\tan x + 2)\). So the integrand \(= \dfrac{\sec^2 x}{\tan x + 2}\). Let \(t = \tan x\), \(dt = \sec^2 x\, dx\).
\(\displaystyle \int \frac{\sec^2 x}{\tan x + 2}\, dx = \int \frac{dt}{t + 2} = \log|\tan x + 2| + c\).

[Textbook answer-key error: the printed key gives the \(x\)-coefficient as \(\frac{11}{75}\); solving \(25A = 11\) gives \(A = \frac{11}{25}\). The answer below is correct.]

Write \(\sin x + 2\cos x = A(3\sin x + 4\cos x) + B(3\cos x - 4\sin x)\), noting \(3\cos x - 4\sin x = \dfrac{d}{dx}(3\sin x + 4\cos x)\).
Comparing coefficients: \(3A - 4B = 1,\ 4A + 3B = 2 \Rightarrow A = \dfrac{11}{25},\ B = \dfrac{2}{25}\).
\(\displaystyle \int \frac{\sin x + 2\cos x}{3\sin x + 4\cos x}\, dx = \frac{11}{25}x + \frac{2}{25}\log|3\sin x + 4\cos x| + c\).

\(\dfrac{1}{2 + 3\tan x} = \dfrac{\cos x}{2\cos x + 3\sin x}\). Write \(\cos x = A(2\cos x + 3\sin x) + B(3\cos x - 2\sin x)\), where \(3\cos x - 2\sin x = \dfrac{d}{dx}(2\cos x + 3\sin x)\).
Comparing: \(2A + 3B = 1,\ 3A - 2B = 0 \Rightarrow A = \dfrac{2}{13},\ B = \dfrac{3}{13}\).
\(\displaystyle \int \frac{1}{2 + 3\tan x}\, dx = \frac{2}{13}x + \frac{3}{13}\log|2\cos x + 3\sin x| + c\).

Divide: \(\dfrac{4e^{x} - 25}{2e^{x} - 5} = 2 - \dfrac{15}{2e^{x} - 5}\). For \(\displaystyle \int \frac{dx}{2e^{x} - 5}\), multiply by \(\dfrac{e^{-x}}{e^{-x}}\) and put \(t = 2 - 5e^{-x}\), \(dt = 5e^{-x}\, dx\):
\(\displaystyle \int \frac{dx}{2e^{x} - 5} = \int \frac{e^{-x}\, dx}{2 - 5e^{-x}} = \frac{1}{5}\log|2 - 5e^{-x}|\).
\(\displaystyle \int \frac{4e^{x} - 25}{2e^{x} - 5}\, dx = 2x - 3\log|2 - 5e^{-x}| + c = 5x - 3\log|2e^{x} - 5| + c\).

[Textbook answer-key error: the printed key gives \(-5x - \log|3e^x - 4|\); both the sign of the linear term and the denominator constant are wrong. The correct answer is \(5x - \log|3e^x + 4|\). The answer below is correct.]

Divide: \(\dfrac{20 + 12e^{x}}{3e^{x} + 4} = 4 + \dfrac{4}{3e^{x} + 4}\). For \(\displaystyle \int \frac{dx}{3e^{x} + 4}\), multiply by \(\dfrac{e^{-x}}{e^{-x}}\) and put \(t = 3 + 4e^{-x}\), \(dt = -4e^{-x}\, dx\):
\(\displaystyle \int \frac{dx}{3e^{x} + 4} = \int \frac{e^{-x}\, dx}{3 + 4e^{-x}} = -\frac{1}{4}\log|3 + 4e^{-x}|\).
\(\displaystyle \int \frac{20 + 12e^{x}}{3e^{x} + 4}\, dx = 4x - \log|3 + 4e^{-x}| + c = 5x - \log|3e^{x} + 4| + c\).

Divide: \(\dfrac{3e^{2x} + 5}{4e^{2x} - 5} = \dfrac{3}{4} + \dfrac{35}{4}\cdot\dfrac{1}{4e^{2x} - 5}\). For \(\displaystyle \int \frac{dx}{4e^{2x} - 5}\), multiply by \(\dfrac{e^{-2x}}{e^{-2x}}\) and put \(t = 4 - 5e^{-2x}\), \(dt = 10e^{-2x}\, dx\):
\(\displaystyle \int \frac{dx}{4e^{2x} - 5} = \int \frac{e^{-2x}\, dx}{4 - 5e^{-2x}} = \frac{1}{10}\log|4 - 5e^{-2x}|\).
\(\displaystyle \int \frac{3e^{2x} + 5}{4e^{2x} - 5}\, dx = \frac{3}{4}x + \frac{7}{8}\log|4 - 5e^{-2x}| + c = -x + \frac{7}{8}\log|4e^{2x} - 5| + c\).

Write \(\cos^8 x\,\cot x = \dfrac{\cos^9 x}{\sin x}\). Let \(t = \sin x\), \(dt = \cos x\, dx\), and \(\cos^8 x = (1 - \sin^2 x)^4 = (1 - t^2)^4\).
\(\displaystyle \int \frac{\cos^9 x}{\sin x}\, dx = \int \frac{(1 - t^2)^4}{t}\, dt = \int \left(\frac{1}{t} - 4t + 6t^3 - 4t^5 + t^7\right) dt\).
\(\displaystyle = \log|\sin x| - 2\sin^2 x + \frac{3}{2}\sin^4 x - \frac{2}{3}\sin^6 x + \frac{1}{8}\sin^8 x + c\).

\(\tan^5 x = \tan^3 x(\sec^2 x - 1) = \tan^3 x\,\sec^2 x - \tan^3 x\), and \(\tan^3 x = \tan x(\sec^2 x - 1) = \tan x\,\sec^2 x - \tan x\).
Integrating term by term (using \(\int \tan^k x\,\sec^2 x\, dx = \tfrac{\tan^{k+1} x}{k+1}\) and \(\int \tan x\, dx = \log|\sec x|\)):
\(\displaystyle \int \tan^5 x\, dx = \frac{\tan^4 x}{4} - \frac{\tan^2 x}{2} + \log|\sec x| + c\).

\(\cos^7 x = (\cos^2 x)^3\cos x = (1 - \sin^2 x)^3\cos x\). Let \(t = \sin x\), \(dt = \cos x\, dx\).
\(\displaystyle \int \cos^7 x\, dx = \int (1 - t^2)^3\, dt = \int \big(1 - 3t^2 + 3t^4 - t^6\big)\, dt = t - t^3 + \frac{3}{5}t^5 - \frac{1}{7}t^7\).
\(\displaystyle = \sin x - \sin^3 x + \frac{3}{5}\sin^5 x - \frac{1}{7}\sin^7 x + c\).

Since \(3x = 2x + x\), \(\tan 3x = \dfrac{\tan 2x + \tan x}{1 - \tan 2x\,\tan x}\), which rearranges to \(\tan 3x\,\tan 2x\,\tan x = \tan 3x - \tan 2x - \tan x\).
\(\displaystyle \int \tan 3x\,\tan 2x\,\tan x\, dx = \int (\tan 3x - \tan 2x - \tan x)\, dx = \frac{1}{3}\log|\sec 3x| - \frac{1}{2}\log|\sec 2x| - \log|\sec x| + c\).

[Textbook answer-key error: the printed key gives \(\frac{1}{6}\cos^{11}x - \frac{1}{9}\cos^9 x + \frac{1}{13}\cos^{13}x\); the \(\cos^{11}x\) coefficient should be \(\frac{2}{11}\) and the \(\cos^{13}x\) term should be negative. The answer below is correct.]

\(\sin^5 x = (\sin^2 x)^2\sin x = (1 - \cos^2 x)^2\sin x\). Let \(t = \cos x\), \(dt = -\sin x\, dx\).
\(\displaystyle \int \sin^5 x\,\cos^8 x\, dx = -\int (1 - t^2)^2\, t^8\, dt = -\int \big(t^8 - 2t^{10} + t^{12}\big)\, dt = -\frac{t^9}{9} + \frac{2t^{11}}{11} - \frac{t^{13}}{13}\).
\(\displaystyle = -\frac{\cos^9 x}{9} + \frac{2\cos^{11} x}{11} - \frac{\cos^{13} x}{13} + c\).

\(\sin 2x = 2\sin x\cos x\). Let \(t = \cos^2 x\), so \(dt = 2\cos x(-\sin x)\, dx = -\sin 2x\, dx\), i.e. \(\sin 2x\, dx = -dt\).
\(\displaystyle \int 3^{\cos^2 x}\,\sin 2x\, dx = \int 3^{t}(-dt) = -\frac{3^{t}}{\log 3} = -\frac{3^{\cos^2 x}}{\log 3} + c\).

Since \(6x = 10x - 4x\), \(\sin 6x = \sin 10x\cos 4x - \cos 10x\sin 4x\). Dividing by \(\sin 10x\,\sin 4x\):
\(\dfrac{\sin 6x}{\sin 10x\,\sin 4x} = \dfrac{\cos 4x}{\sin 4x} - \dfrac{\cos 10x}{\sin 10x} = \cot 4x - \cot 10x\).
\(\displaystyle \int (\cot 4x - \cot 10x)\, dx = \frac{1}{4}\log|\sin 4x| - \frac{1}{10}\log|\sin 10x| + c\).

[Textbook answer-key error: the printed key writes \(\frac{1}{2}\log\big[(1+\cos^2 x) - \cos^2 x\big]\), placing the \(-\cos^2 x\) inside the log (which would collapse to \(\frac{1}{2}\log 1 = 0\)); it belongs outside, as \(\frac{1}{2}\log(1+\cos^2 x) - \frac{1}{2}\cos^2 x\). The answer below is correct.]

Let \(t = \cos x\), so \(dt = -\sin x\, dx\) and \(\cos^3 x = t^3\).
\(\displaystyle \int \frac{\sin x\,\cos^3 x}{1 + \cos^2 x}\, dx = -\int \frac{t^3}{1 + t^2}\, dt = -\int \left(t - \frac{t}{1 + t^2}\right) dt = -\frac{t^2}{2} + \frac{1}{2}\log(1 + t^2)\).
\(\displaystyle = \frac{1}{2}\log(1 + \cos^2 x) - \frac{1}{2}\cos^2 x + c\).
